findings.title: Retained outcome evidence remains a cross-specification dependency
Generic task-control and lifecycle observability are materially strengthened
Supervising-principal and delegated authority remain profile/governance dependencies
Application-state namespace is not an authorization boundary
Removal evidence does not guarantee durable redress delivery
Relationship publication provenance and correlation control are explicit

disposition.summary: Trust Tasks through cdfc6e2 is net assurance-strengthening: framework 0.5 tightens freshness/privacy/lifecycle semantics, application-state adds explicit concurrency controls, relationship publication binds issuer authority while minimizing correlation, and removal notices strengthen adverse-decision evidence. Residual gaps remain at cross-spec outcome/delegation, deployment isolation and durable redress delivery boundaries.

evidence.description: Pinned upstream Trust Tasks revision cdfc6e231dc6cc9ed901bbd27b4c6e8ea2f3e06a and descendant compare window from the prior reviewed baseline

retest_triggers: material Trust Tasks change after cdfc6e2 affecting authority, lifecycle, replay, privacy or redress
relationship publication proof-of-possession or retention change
removal-notice delivery or post-removal redress profile change
Credential or ZKP composition change affecting action-time authority or privacy
